items.title: Chamath Palihapitiya Sounds Alarm on AI Coding: "We Are Turning an Entire Generation" Into "Slot Machines"
items.note: Published September 21, 2026, this piece covers Chamath's X posts warning that bottoms up AI coding tool adoption is turning developers into the equivalent of retirees pushing a button in front of casino slot machines. He argued effective AI adoption requires top down leadership from executives.

items.title: The case for Socratic inquiry in the classroom
items.note: Neos Kosmos published this opinion piece on September 21, 2026 arguing for Socratic questioning in schools, describing Socrates as a gadfly who stirred Athens out of its complacency and applying that model to today's classrooms.

items.title: Bill Gurley: Searching for Feynman (All-In Summit 2026)
items.note: Gurley delivered this talk at the All-In Summit on September 19, 2026, comparing Richard Feynman's Challenger Commission work, the Boeing 737 MAX MCAS failure, and AI as three different responses to institutional accountability failure. A transcript ran on The Singju Post.

items.title: 12 Conversations (Ryuichi Sakamoto & Alva Noto)
items.note: Noton released this collaborative album of piano and electronics dialogues between Sakamoto and Carsten Nicolai on September 18, 2026, recorded during the 2022 sessions for Sakamoto's final solo album 12.

items.title: Review: Ryuichi Sakamoto & Alva Noto - 12 Conversations
items.note: German outlet Musikexpress reviewed 12 Conversations following its September 18, 2026 release, describing it as amplifying the somber, reflective mood of Sakamoto's 12 and calling it one of the most emotionally open records in Nicolai's catalog.

items.title: Segundo G.H. leva universo de Clarice Lispector a danca no Festival Mulheres em Cena
items.note: Dancer Carina Nagib presented this solo piece freely inspired by Lispector's A Paixao Segundo G.H. on September 18, 2026 at the Centro de Referencia da Danca in Sao Paulo, part of the 10th Festival Mulheres em Cena.

items.title: Forbes 400: The 10 Richest Women In America 2026
items.note: Forbes reported on September 17, 2026 that Anthropic president Daniela Amodei, 39, entered the Forbes 400 for the first time with an estimated 15.5 billion dollar fortune, making her the youngest woman on the list.

items.title: Almost Every Job Has Tasks That AI Can Change
items.note: Stanford GSB Insights published this piece around September 17, 2026 featuring economist Erik Brynjolfsson arguing that AI's transformation of work is only beginning and that institutions are not yet prepared for it.

items.title: A Blueprint for Keeping Humans in Control of AI
items.note: Stanford GSB Insights piece from September 2026 covers research by PhD student William Overman and professor Mohsen Bayati using game theory and reinforcement learning to design oversight frameworks for autonomous AI agents.

items.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has a flawed view of AI regulation, heavyweight tech investor Bill Gurley warns
items.note: Published around mid-September 2026, this piece reports Gurley's public criticism of Dario Amodei's AI regulation proposal, arguing that regulatory capture caused failures like the Boeing 737 MAX crashes and that any AI regulator needs real authority over the companies it oversees.

items.title: Dirtbag Billionaire: How Yvon Chouinard Built Patagonia, Made a Fortune, and Gave It All Away (paperback)
items.note: David Gelles' biography of Chouinard was released in paperback on September 15, 2026, prompting renewed press coverage of Chouinard's life and Patagonia's 2022 ownership giveaway.

items.title: "This was surreal" (on Trump's live call-in to Jensen Huang at the All-In Summit)
items.note: Chamath posted this reaction on X after President Trump phoned into the All-In Summit stage during Jensen Huang's session on September 14, 2026, dismissing AI and data center backlash as a hoax.

items.title: Jensen Huang: The Doomer Hoax, Superintelligence Is Here, and The Future of AI (ft. President Trump)
items.note: Chamath co-hosted this All-In Summit episode on September 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, in which Jensen Huang argued AI doomerism is overstated and President Trump joined the stage by surprise phone call.

items.title: Montemor-o-Novo assinala 70 anos de Grande Sertao: Veredas
items.note: Published September 14, 2026, this piece covers a session at the Biblioteca Municipal Almeida Faria in Montemor-o-Novo, Portugal marking the 70th anniversary of Grande Sertao: Veredas, part of a wider Portugal program running September 7 to 11 across Montemor-o-Novo, Lisbon and Loule.

items.title: What Amodei's AI slowdown could mean for Anthropic's imminent IPO
items.note: CNBC reported on September 14, 2026 that Amodei's pacing essay creates tension with Anthropic's push toward a roughly 2 trillion dollar IPO on Nasdaq, centering on how his public safety warnings intersect with the company's imminent listing.

items.title: Chamath Palihapitiya: Anthropic Employee's "Human Extinction" AI Warning Risks $2.3 Trillion IPO
items.note: Published September 13, 2026, this piece reports Chamath's comments on the September 11 All-In episode that a departing Anthropic safety researcher's human extinction warning turned a routine IPO quiet period into a live disclosure crisis.

items.title: We Must Pace the Frontier
items.note: Dario Amodei published this essay on September 12, 2026 arguing the AI industry should deliberately slow the pace of capability improvements, with Anthropic unilaterally committing to give outside evaluators permanent, employee level access.

items.title: CBS News Sunday Morning: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on AI risk
items.note: In an interview aired September 12, 2026, Amodei said AI's exponential growth is a warning sign the industry needs to slow down, and said the industry had understated the technology's risks for too long.

items.title: Grande Sertao: Veredas, de Guimaraes Rosa, a advocacia e a IA que ia, veio
items.note: Jornal Opcao essay published September 11, 2026 marks the novel's 70th anniversary and connects its themes to law and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Dia do Cerrado: Guimaraes Rosa denunciou riscos ao bioma, diz biologa
items.note: Agencia Brasil piece tied to Cerrado Day, September 11, 2026, argues that Guimaraes Rosa's writing anticipated environmental risks to the Cerrado biome, according to an interviewed biologist.

items.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto: seeing sound, hearing time
items.note: Sakamoto's first major European retrospective opened September 11, 2026 at Hamburger Bahnhof Berlin, spanning 1,500 square meters with sound installations made with Shiro Takatani, Carsten Nicolai and Apichatpong Weerasethakul, running through May 23, 2027.

items.title: No. 26: Dario and Daniela Amodei: The Jewish siblings shaping AI's next frontier
items.note: Jerusalem Post profile, published around September 10, 2026, ranks the Amodei siblings on its 50 Most Influential Jews list and discusses Daniela's role as Anthropic president overseeing safety and trust.

items.title: Michelle Obama gets warm welcome at US Open during star-studded semifinal night
items.note: Michelle Obama attended the US Open women's semifinals at Arthur Ashe Stadium on September 10, 2026, seated among other notable attendees including Al Roker, Hoda Kotb and Robin Roberts.

items.title: CEO Speaker Series With Dario Amodei of Anthropic
items.note: Amodei appeared at the Council on Foreign Relations around September 9, 2026 to discuss U.S. AI leadership, innovation amid strategic competition, and the outlook for frontier model development.

items.title: The Socrates Agent
items.note: Writer Daniel Miessler published this piece on September 8, 2026 describing an AI agent design modeled on the Socratic method, built to teach by asking questions rather than giving answers.

items.title: Music Sets You Free: A Memoir
items.note: HarperVia published the first English translation, by Sam Bett, of Sakamoto's two Japanese memoirs combined as Music Sets You Free, with the Japan Times review running September 7 ahead of the book's release.

items.title: O Ovo e a Galinha, new solo stage adaptation
items.note: A new solo stage adaptation of Lispector's 1964 story O Ovo e a Galinha, directed by Joana Medeiros and performed by Ana Hartmann, premiered September 4, 2026 at Teatro Ziembinski in Rio de Janeiro and runs through September 27.

items.title: Simplesmente eu, Clarice Lispector (Beth Goulart, Sao Paulo season)
items.note: Actress Beth Goulart's long running monologue about Lispector's life and work continues its extended Sao Paulo season at Teatro Moise Safra, running through September 27, 2026.

items.title: Patagonia Joins Lawsuit Against Trump's Order Shrinking Utah National Monuments
items.note: On September 2, 2026, Patagonia, the company Chouinard founded, sued the Trump administration with seven environmental and Indigenous rights groups over its July 2026 order cutting Bears Ears National Monument by roughly 91 percent.

items.title: How Smart Leaders Build Trust
items.note: Stanford GSB Insights article published September 2, 2026 features the JetBlue chairman on building a high trust organizational culture, with seven practical tips for leaders.

items.title: You Need to Learn to Say No (Even to an Inauguration) with Taraji P. Henson
items.note: IMO episode with Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson released August 28, 2026, featuring Taraji P. Henson on setting boundaries, why Michelle skipped a presidential inauguration, and post White House therapy.

items.title: How AI could uncover the hidden ways people work together
items.note: Published late August 2026, this Stanford Report piece covers GSB professor Amir Goldberg and PhD candidate Yankai Wang's award winning large coordination model research from the Stanford HAI and Google DeepMind AI for Organizations Grand Challenge.

items.title: Naspers exec pay under fire as shareholders vote against policy again
items.note: At the Naspers AGM on August 26, 2026, ordinary N shareholders again voted non-bindingly against the remuneration policy covering CEO Fabricio Bloisi, roughly 74 percent opposed, though the resolution passed due to the high vote A shares.

items.title: Anthropic to Grant CEO Amodei Extra Voting Power Ahead of IPO, Report Says
items.note: Report names Daniela Amodei among the seven Anthropic co-founders, including her brother Dario, set to receive supervoting shares ahead of the company's planned IPO since combined founder ownership has diluted to roughly 2 percent.

items.title: Michelle Obama Talks Fashion to Sold-Out Island Crowds
items.note: Coverage of Michelle Obama's sold out Martha's Vineyard Author Series appearance on August 23, 2026 for her new book The Look, discussing media scrutiny of her clothing and body during the Obama presidency.

items.title: Os 70 anos de Grande sertao: Veredas chegam ao Museu da Lingua Portuguesa
items.note: On August 22, 2026 the Museu da Lingua Portuguesa in Sao Paulo held panels with writers Milton Hatoum, Jeferson Tenorio and Socorro Acioli marking 70 years of Grande Sertao: Veredas, alongside a Companhia das Letras commemorative edition.

items.title: Socrates' Turf
items.note: Merve Emre interviews philosopher Agnes Callard for a New York Review of Books online series on the interview form, discussing the Socratic dialogue as a model Callard calls the philosopher's interview, published August 18, 2026.

items.title: Rio de Clarice: filme adapta cinco contos de Clarice Lispector
items.note: The film Rio de Clarice opened in Brazilian theaters on August 13, adapting five Lispector short stories through five Brazilian filmmakers, with a script co-written by her grand niece Nicole Allgranti and biographer Teresa Montero.

items.title: REG - Prosus NV Naspers Limited - Director/PDMR Shareholding
items.note: Regulatory disclosure dated August 12, 2026 covering Fabricio Bloisi's exercise and sale of Naspers and linked Prosus share options ahead of their August 2026 expiry.

items.title: Fabricio Bloisi: e possivel criar algo grande do nada
items.note: In an August 2026 interview with Seja Relevante, a Fundacao Dom Cabral platform, Bloisi said entrepreneurs who anticipate the world five years out can achieve more than in the previous fifteen, citing Movile's near bankruptcies before it became a major Latin American tech company.

items.title: Yvon Chouinard Was Destroying the Mountains He Loved. He Made 1 Painful Decision That Built the Patagonia Empire
items.note: Inc. piece published August 4, 2026 revisiting Chouinard's decision to abandon pitons, the environmental call that reshaped his business decades before sustainability became a buzzword.

items.title: Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers, not specialists, in the AI era
items.note: On Lenny's Podcast, Netflix Chief Product and Technology Officer Elizabeth Stone explains why Netflix is hiring more systems thinkers who can work across business domains rather than narrow specialists, and describes AI fluency as a universal expectation across the company.

items.title: Netflix wants 'AI fluency' from everyone, but craft is still scarce
items.note: This piece recaps Elizabeth Stone's comments that AI fluency means an experimentation mindset plus judgment about where AI helps, while deep craft in engineering, data science and design remains scarce and increasingly valuable.
